title: Fats Navarro and Dizzy's calculated image
summary: He praises Fats Navarro as lyrical like Armstrong, while Dizzy wants to shock and chose his image, with an Ellington story about picking the right notes.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution

blocks.x: Now, what did you think of Fats Navarro?

Beautiful. That's what I'm talking about you understand what I mean?
Like, I'll go back to Duke, like before, I says there are too many notes in here and he says yes, well, I can't play them, he says be sure that you pick the right ones and he was bugging him about those notes.
That meant, that if you don't make that right note, I'm going to run you out of here. Boy played the -- as beautiful as he could play it and play all the notes -/ he was a lyrical man. See? Louis Armstrong was a lyrical man.
Dizzy is a man -- he want's to shock you -- he wants to -- that's why he put the horn up there. That's Dizzy.

You understand?
But see, fool a fool and Dizzy's the wisest fox going, that's how you do it. You got to have some type of image. Dizzy chose that. I'm going to do that.
